trust_decision.summary: The Ruby block is passed to SQLite as raw C user data ((void *)block) and is kept alive only by a per-database container. The published fix makes that container an Array and pushes every block, so re-registering a name with a different arity can no longer drop the sole Ruby reference to a block that SQLite still holds in a separate FuncDef. Decided at the single C write site (rb_hash_aset -> rb_ary_push) plus the container's Ruby default ({} -> []).

landing_point.why: Anyone reading 'use-after-free when redefining SQLite functions with different arity' looks at define_function_with_flags, where the block is passed to sqlite3_create_function and then stored by name; the rb_hash_aset there is the one line that loses the old block on redefinition.

fix_sites.entry_point: SQLite3::Database#define_function (C, registered ext/sqlite3/database.c:967) and SQLite3::Database#define_function_with_flags (C, registered ext/sqlite3/database.c:968), both through define_function_with_flags at ext/sqlite3/database.c:503
SQLite3::Database#initialize (Database.new), whose @functions default is the keep-alive container written by the C extension; callers arrive via #create_function at lib/sqlite3/database.rb:412

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The Ruby site is only an ivar default in the pure-Ruby constructor, in another language and directory from the C extension where the memory bug lives, so it reads as unrelated to a use-after-free.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Re-registering a name must stay legal: same-arity redefinition must replace the body (loop of define_function('hello') { |a| thing }, test/test_database.rb:508-513), and a different-arity registration must coexist, leaving the earlier arity callable ('select f(1)' still returns the original block, fix.diff:48-54; aggregate analogue with GC.start between registrations, test/test_integration_aggregate.rb:356-365). A fix that raises on a duplicate name or deletes the earlier registration breaks one of these.

O6_input_shapes: same name re-registered with a different fixed block arity (1 then 2), the shape in the advisory and in fix.diff:48-54
variadic block (arity -1) versus fixed arity for the same name

same name and arity re-registered with a different text_rep encoding (SQLITE_UTF8 vs SQLITE_UTF16*/UTF16), which SQLite keeps as a separate function entry; the array keeps every block, a [name, arity]-keyed hash would not
create_function's wrapper proc is always variadic (-1, lib/sqlite3/database.rb:413), so mixing create_function with define_function on one name also leaves an entry behind

O8b_injection_room.sibling: collation() stores the comparator VALUE in a name-keyed single-slot hash with the comment 'Make sure our comparator doesn't get garbage collected.'
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is literally the same keep-alive shape and the same comment as the buggy @functions hash; a maintainer adding a text_rep/encoding argument to collation, or a second collation registry, would reproduce the redefinition UAF.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the aggregate registry already uses -aggregators as an Array and has the multi-arity GC test (test/test_integration_aggregate.rb:356-365)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same mechanism done correctly in the same repo; a sibling that reverts one aggregator registry to a name-keyed hash (e.g. a per-connection subclass registry) is exactly what the scalar path looked like at the pinned commit.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: create_function composes a fresh wrapper proc per call and stores it in the same container
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Any solver-visible fix at this wrapper (e.g. caching one wrapper per name to avoid allocation) re-creates the single-reference problem independently of the C site.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: set_authorizer keeps the callback in a single @authorizer slot passed as (void *)self
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same 'callback must outlive the C registration' pattern; a maintainer extending it to a per-action or per-name authorizer table would store one proc per key.

O9_family: use-after-free (CWE-416) of a GC-managed Ruby callable held as raw C user data

O10_build.toolchain: Ruby + mkmf/gcc/make; packaged build uses mini_portile2 to build SQLite 3.53.2 (dependencies.yml:10-13, downloads sqlite-autoconf-3530200.tar.gz from sqlite.org), or --enable-system-libraries with libsqlite3-dev; minitest + rake
O10_build.project_tests: minitest via rake test; test/test_database.rb covers custom functions (test_define_function:457, test_function_return_types:508, test_function_gc_segfault:515) on a :memory: database (test/test_database.rb:16); test/test_integration_aggregate.rb covers the aggregate UAF siblings (:142, :356, :367)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Change rb_hash_aset to rb_ary_push in the C extension only and leave the Ruby @functions = {} default (TypeError), or keep a Hash keyed by [name, arity], which still drops blocks re-registered under a different text_rep encoding.

out_of_scope_notes: Related but outside this advisory: create_function(name, arity, ...) ignores its arity argument because the wrapper proc at lib/sqlite3/database.rb:413 is always variadic (-1); not pursued.
